To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the web-based groupware progress reporting mechanism evolved in three distinct ways: (1) it evolved from an individual report to a group report, (2) it evolved from a report that was submitted at the end of the project to a report that was updated at the end of each week of the project, and (3) it evolved from being a report to being an online discussion forum.

the evolution of the progress reporting mechanism in the web-based groupware system was driven by three major factors: (a) changes to the pedagogical context of the courses, (b) the evolution of the web-based group ware system itself and (c) the evolution of students’ expectations and demands.

(1) the genre of project progress reports in the electronic environment has evolved over the last three semesters, (2) the evolution of this genre is related to changes in the structure of the course, (3) the evolution of the genre is related to the structure of the genre, and (4) there are differences between the genre of the project progress reports and the genre of the course.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution and use of the genre structuring in a Web-based groupware medium, and the implications of this evolution for the teaching and learning of Information Technology.
the evolution of the genre of the project progress report from a paper based to an electronic based medium.
the evolution of a genre, in this case the project progress report.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genre structuring is not a one-way street.
the genre of the project progress report has not changed in its essence, but has evolved in its structure and its use.
genre structuring in web-based applications is a complex process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genre structuring of the project progress reporting mechanism is not a simple one-to-one mapping of the paper-based genre to its electronic counterpart.
the evolution of this reporting mechanism has been a process of gradual refinement, and that this evolution has occurred in a number of stages.
the genre structure of the original paper based project progress report has not changed significantly in its electronic version.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genre structuring framework can be used to analyze the evolution of genre in a web-based medium.

, in order for the web-based groupware mechanism to be effective, the instructor needs to provide a clear and detailed template for the project progress report, and the students need to be trained on its use.
the genre structuring approach can be applied successfully to the study of genre evolution in a web-based environment, and the results obtained can be used to improve teaching practice.
